title: How much longer is one piece of cloth than the other?
description: Two lengths of cloth, three point five metres and two point seven metres, are lined up with point under point. One unit is broken into ten tenths so the tenths can be taken away, and the same answer comes from the mixed fractions. Keeko's doubt takes the smaller digit from the larger in each place.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the tenths on top are fewer, break one unit into ten tenths and then subtract place by place. Watch for students who take the smaller digit from the larger and ignore which number is on top.

source: Shylaja needs 3.5 m of cloth and Priya needs 2.7 m. How much
video_script.why: The child added decimals with carries and now subtracts them, borrowing where the tenths are too few.
video_script.substitution: Line up the point, break one unit into ten tenths when the tenths are too few, and subtract place by place.
video_script.anchor: Two pieces of cloth from the book: one for a kurti, three point five metres, and one for a skirt, two point seven metres.
video_script.wrong_move: Takes five from seven and two from three, the smaller digit from the larger in each place, instead of breaking a unit.
video_script.payoff_line: Break one unit into ten tenths when the tenths are too few
maths_rules: tenths: 5 is less than 7, so break 1 unit of the 3 into 10 tenths
3 becomes 2 units, and 5 tenths become 15 tenths
the slip: 7 - 5 = 2 and 3 - 2 = 1 gives 1.2, but the pieces differ by less than 1 m
video_script.design: The two pieces of cloth stay as the anchor. The working band builds the column subtraction one place at a time, with the borrowed unit shown as ten tenths.

narration: <bookmark mark='setup'/>Step one, write three point five above two point seven, with point under point.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>We subtract, because we are finding how much longer the first piece is.

narration: <bookmark mark='few'/>Step two, look at the tenths.
Five tenths are fewer than seven tenths.
<bookmark mark='break'/>Break one unit of the three into ten tenths, because we cannot take seven from five.
<bookmark mark='new'/>The three becomes two units, and five tenths become fifteen tenths.

beats.on_screen: 15 tenths - 7 tenths = 8 tenths; 2 units - 2 units = 0 units

marks.tenths: 15 - 7 = 8 is written under the tenths column
marks.units: 2 - 2 = 0 is written under the units column

narration: <bookmark mark='tenths'/>Step three, subtract place by place.
Fifteen tenths take away seven tenths leaves eight tenths.
<bookmark mark='units'/>Two units take away two units leaves no units.

marks.frac: the mixed fraction 3 5/10 is written beside the column

narration: <bookmark mark='frac'/>Step four, check with fractions, as your book does.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Three and five tenths is the same as two and fifteen tenths.
<bookmark mark='sub2'/>Two and fifteen tenths take away two and seven tenths leaves eight tenths, the same as before.

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Break one unit into ten tenths when the tenths are too few.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_2}}'s cloth is zero point eight metre longer than {{NAME_3}}'s.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the difference is one point two, taking five from seven and two from three.
<bookmark mark='far'/>But the pieces differ by less than one metre, so one point two is too long.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Seven tenths cannot be taken from five tenths, so we must break a unit first.
